text:
aline: Quick heads-up — during the 4-bit bring-up for reranker-v2 I observed +0.02 NDCG on dev but -0.06 on our prod-like holdout. Something smells like eval leakage from candidate dedupe.

matt: Can you repro locally against the holdout? What exactly do you mean by ‘dedupe’ here?

aline: Yep repro'd locally. Our candidate pipeline dedupes by URL+title fingerprint but keeps the candidate with the highest pre-score. The pre-score comes from an older training scorer, so we end up keeping a candidate that was favored by the training scorer — effectively leaking signal into eval.

sasha: Oof. Is this only when using preprocess v1 candidate-merge? I thought v2 changed the policy.

aline: Looks correlated. Preproc v1 uses score_max to pick which duplicate to keep; preproc v2 uses stable sort + keep-first (score-agnostic). The 4-bit quantization causes small reranker score perturbations, which affects ordering and makes the leakage manifest as a larger NDCG delta on holdout.

kevin: Can you paste the repro command + a minimal sample of the candidate JSON so we can eyeball it?

aline: Sure — repro command I ran: 
```bash
# run eval on holdout with score-based dedupe
python eval.py --candidates candidates_prod.jsonl --dedupe_method=score_max --model=/tmp/reranker-4bit.pt --metrics=ndcg,mrr
```

aline: Minimal candidate example (simplified):
```json
[
  {"cid":"c1","url":"https://a.com/x","title":"A","pre_score":12.1},
  {"cid":"c2","url":"https://a.com/x","title":"A","pre_score":5.3},
  {"cid":"c3","url":"https://b.com/y","title":"B","pre_score":1.2}
]
```

zara: So dedupe preferring the higher pre_score will keep c1 (which was privileged by the old scorer). That definitely leaks. Fix idea: use dedupe_method=first or canonical doc id, independent of any model score.

matt: Can you re-run the bring-up with dedupe_method=first and report the deltas? If the quantized model still regresses then it's a real model quality issue; if not, it's an eval artifact.

aline: I'm scheduling that now. Also adding a quick overlap check between train candidate ids and holdout top-K to quantify leak.

kevin: Also add an ablation: compare fp16 vs 4-bit with the same dedupe pipeline so we isolate quantization effect from dedupe leakage.

sasha: Agree. And add a tiny test in the eval harness that fails the run if any holdout query contains candidates that were present in training set (overlap > 0). That will catch these leaks earlier.

aline: Will do both. @ci-bot can you kick off an eval job for holdout with dedupe=first + fp16 vs 4bit ablation?

ci-bot: Started job: eval-holdout-1719999000-dedupe-first-ablation (ETA ~12m). Logs: https://ci.internal/runs/1719999000

zara: Nice. Once we get results we should update the onboarding checklist: “ensure dedupe is scorer-agnostic for eval holdouts”.

matt: Thanks for catching this — could have masked / inflated gains for a while. :eyes:

aline: np — will post results here when the CI completes. :raised_hands:
